text: The Operations Manager, trusting the report again, comes back with something new: can she see what percentage of orders are shipping late, broken out by region and subcategory. That's specific enough to build directly, because late has an exact definition already sitting in data you pulled back in Lesson 3: a ship date after the due date.

The cleanest fix follows the pattern this chapter already established: push the business rule into the staged view. Alter vw_CarrawayWeeklySalesFact to add an IsLate column, computed with a CASE expression comparing ShipDate to DueDate. Because this is the same object from Lesson 4, nothing about the model's relationships breaks. Fact just gains one new column on the next refresh.
Refresh the model in Power BI Desktop and confirm IsLate shows up as a new column on Fact, with values of zero or one.

The new measure, Percent Shipped Late, uses CALCULATE with a simple boolean filter, Fact IsLate equals one, not ALL. That respects whatever region and subcategory filters are already active on the page, instead of stripping them. DIVIDE against the unfiltered Order Count turns it into a rate.

Add it to the Drill-Down page only — as a KPI card and a second value in the existing matrix. The Sales Director never asked for a fulfillment metric, so this stays scoped to the audience that actually needs it. Next lesson: wrapping up everything you built.
